problem_statement:
An application that enables CONFIG_SCHED_EVENTS (and CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT in the observed configuration) and includes nuttx/event.h cannot be built: the kernel has no event group header or symbols. The observed failure is a compilation error: nuttx/event.h: No such file or directory. If the header were present, the expected event-group interfaces would still be undefined.

The kernel must provide a kernel event group synchronization primitive. An event object represents a set of pending events as a bit mask and allows tasks to block until one or more specified events are posted. The missing interface must include the public header nuttx/event.h, the event object type nxevent_t, and the initializer macro NXEVENT_INITIALIZER(event, initial_mask), where initial_mask is the initial pending event set.

Required behavior: nxevent_init(event, events) initializes the event object and sets the pending event mask to events. nxevent_destroy(event) destroys the object and must unblock any tasks waiting on it. nxevent_reset(event, events) updates the pending event mask to the supplied value and wakes waiters whose conditions are met; a zero mask uses the same any/all wake-up convention as posting. nxevent_post(event, events, flags) delivers events to the object; by default it merges the supplied mask into the current pending mask, a zero event mask is treated as an any delivery and must wake blocked waiters immediately, and a successful call returns 0.

nxevent_wait(event, events, flags) blocks until the requested condition is satisfied and returns the matching event mask. If events is 0, the condition is any pending event. If NXEVENT_WAIT_ALL is set, all bits in events must be pending; otherwise any bit in events may satisfy the wait. By default, the events returned by a successful wait are cleared from the pending mask. nxevent_tickwait(event, events, flags, ticks) has the same condition behavior but returns after a timeout in ticks; ticks equal to zero is equivalent to a non-blocking try-wait, and it returns the matched mask on success or 0 on timeout/no match. nxevent_trywait(event, events, flags) is the non-blocking form and returns the matched mask if the condition is already satisfied, otherwise 0.

The implementation must support multiple waiters on the same event object. A posting must wake each waiting task whose any/all condition becomes satisfied. A task waiting without NXEVENT_WAIT_ALL should return only the pending bits it matched, while a task waiting with NXEVENT_WAIT_ALL should return only when all requested bits are pending. Events consumed by a waiting task should not satisfy later waits unless re-posted. The posting, reset, and destroy operations must be able to unblock waiters in a safe manner, including when delivery occurs from interrupt context.

On the old kernel these symbols and the CONFIG_SCHED_EVENTS option do not exist, so the test does not build; the task is to provide the kernel nxevent event-group facility so the test compiles and its assertions pass.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: When ostest is built with CONFIG_SCHED_EVENTS=y and CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT=y, the test change compiles nxevent.c and invokes nxevent_test from ostest_main. That test includes <nuttx/event.h> and expects the kernel event-group API, including nxevent_t, NXEVENT_INITIALIZER, nxevent_init, nxevent_destroy, nxevent_reset, nxevent_post, nxevent_wait, nxevent_tickwait, and nxevent_trywait, along with flags such as NXEVENT_WAIT_ALL. With the base kernel, the build fails with a missing-header error for nuttx/event.h, so nxevent_test cannot be built or run. The observed problem is therefore a missing public event-group interface in the kernel when the event configuration is enabled. The expected behavior is that the kernel supports the event-group semantics exercised by the test: initialization and reset of event masks, posting that merges or sets events, waiting for any or all specified events, trywait/tickwait returning the matching events or zero when not satisfied, and posting waking waiting tasks, including lower-priority tasks, as exercised by nxevent_test.
